requirements.evidence: Every requirement and contract item is implemented. Queue::DEFAULT_PREFIX_MAP, defaultPrefixFor() with range fallback and prefixForPriority() are at app/Models/Queue.php:24-108. Map validation runs on every save through static::saving (Queue.php:28-31): canonical keys via ctype_digit plus a round-trip check, '/^[A-Z]\z/' values, uniqueness of custom letters plus uncovered defaults, and an empty map normalized to null. The array cast is added and the map is not in #[Fillable]. Ticket::nextCode(Queue, priority, issueDate) is scoped by issue_date, uses a LIKE on the prefix, orders by id desc, skips malformed codes with \d{3,} and falls back to <prefix>001 (app/Models/Ticket.php:35-53). IssueTicket reads now() once and uses it for the code day, issued_at and issue_date (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:44-57). The factory derives issue_date from issued_at, allocates the code for that day and priority, keeps explicit codes and rejects a misaligned issue_date (database/factories/TicketFactory.php:44-66). The migration adds the column nullable, backfills from DATE(issued_at), makes it NOT NULL, swaps the unique index and has a guarded down(). UpdateQueue gets priorityPrefixMap, validates it before any assignment and rethrows as ValidationException('priority_prefix_map') (app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:30-36). Docs and CHANGELOG are updated. Two small risks: on MySQL, dropping unique(queue_id, code) before adding the new index can fail if that index backs the queue_id foreign key; and the 'date:Y-m-d' custom cast stores whatever raw value is assigned.

conventions.evidence: The domain write goes through the existing UpdateQueue action, and authorization stays in Gate::forUser($actor)->authorize('update', $queue). No service layer is added. The map is not added to #[Fillable(...)], and system fields are written with forceCreate as before. The migrations have generator-style timestamps and reversible down() methods. PHPDoc is updated on nextCode, UpdateQueue and the new Queue methods. business-rules.md, database-schema.md (ER diagram and notes) and CHANGELOG [Unreleased] Added/Changed are all updated.

security.evidence: No Livewire or HTTP surface is touched. The map is not mass-assignable (Queue.php:13 Fillable is unchanged), is validated in the model on every save and in UpdateQueue before any assignment, and owner/admin authorization is kept and tested (PriorityPrefixTest 'keeps owner and admin authorization'). The prefix is interpolated into a regex in nextCode, but it can only be a validated A-Z letter or a default, so this is safe.

tests.evidence: The tests are broad. tests/Feature/PriorityPrefixTest.php covers default and range fallback, custom map precedence, valid and invalid keys ('foo', -1, '010', '1.5'), invalid values, duplicate effective letters ({'0':'E'}, {'5':'N'}), null normalization on every save, UpdateQueue set/keep/clear, rejection without partial update, employee/outsider denial, and the NOT NULL and unique (queue, code, issue_date) constraints. IssueTicketTest adds per-priority prefixes, a custom map, independent sequences, a daily restart, the midnight single-clock case, legacy A codes, and malformed N-X codes. TicketFactoryTest covers issue_date derivation, past-day allocation, priority/custom prefixes, explicit code and the misalignment rejection. Existing tests were updated to the new N codes, not weakened. Missing: no test for the migration backfill or its down() guard.

simplicity.evidence: The change is lean and reuses the existing nextCode/UpdateQueue/factory structure. One normalizePriorityPrefixMap function serves both the saving hook and UpdateQueue. The extra parseCanonicalKey helper and the factory's InvalidArgumentException on a mismatched issue_date add a little code beyond the minimum, but both serve stated requirements.

readability.evidence: Names are clear (defaultPrefixFor, normalizePriorityPrefixMap, parseCanonicalKey) and methods are small. The comments explain the reasons behind decisions, e.g. the single clock read in IssueTicket.php:42-43 and the 'date:Y-m-d' storage note in Ticket.php:129. Style is consistent with sibling code, with no dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: Every file serves the task: models, actions, factories, two migrations, docs, CHANGELOG and tests. The QueueFactory default 'priority_prefix_map' => null is needed for the contract. There are no unrelated refactors.

issues.explanation: On MySQL, dropping unique(queue_id, code) before creating unique(queue_id, code, issue_date) can fail (error 1553) if that index is the only one backing the queue_id foreign key; creating the new index first would avoid this.
No test covers the migration backfill of issue_date from DATE(issued_at) or the down() guard against duplicated codes.

The custom 'date:Y-m-d' cast bypasses Eloquent's date normalization on write, so assigning a Carbon or datetime string to issue_date stores it raw, and the string comparison in nextCode's where('issue_date', ...) could then miss rows.

After ksort, a map with only sequential keys such as [0 => 'X'] is JSON-encoded as a list ("[\"X\"]") instead of the documented object form; it decodes back to the same array, so the behavior is unaffected.

review.summary: The change adds priority-based code prefixes (N/P/E) with a validated per-queue override map, scopes code sequences to a new issue_date column restarting daily, updates IssueTicket, TicketFactory and UpdateQueue to match, and updates docs and the changelog with thorough Pest tests. The requirements, contract and edge cases (canonical keys, effective-letter uniqueness, malformed and legacy codes, the midnight clock) are covered and conventions are followed. Remaining concerns are minor: the order of index operations in the migration on MySQL, and no test for the migration backfill.
